audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was scored for Ryze, Level 6 for Ryze, and 2+ items for Cho'Gath — the last two backwards against the page's own text. whys[4] says Realm Warp is an escape tool and not a kill tool, whys[6] and the late block say two-item Ryze finally threatens his health pool. Separately the page labels this a "Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10" with a green tone while Ryze wins 45.61%.
audit.why: The mirror (chogath__ryze) proposed exactly Level 1 Skill, Level 6 Cho'Gath, 2+ items Ryze as one atomic chart group; the packet agrees on all three. And a 45.6% win rate with Cho'Gath owning four of seven stages is not a favoured lane — the difficulty copy contradicts both the data and the chart.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 4 and 6 flipped in both layers as matched pairs with ratings, and the difficulty framing raised to Hard (7/10, carry threat 7/10) with the tone token moved off green.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spikes name the right abilities but carry no cooldowns, so "commit on its cooldown" has no number behind it anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Rupture is a flat 6s at 950 range; Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 at only 300 range; Feast is 80/70/60. Those three numbers are the whole sequencing problem — his knockup returns faster than your window, but his silence only reaches 300, which is inside your 615 and well inside Overload's 1000.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into the level-3 spike and the cooldown do, with the 300-range silence given as the line you simply do not have to cross.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] and the late block credit Ryze with a "mana shield" that buffers Feast's execute.
audit.why: Ryze has no shield in his kit — Arcane Mastery converts bonus mana into spell damage and AP into maximum mana, nothing more. Any shield here comes from Seraph's Embrace as an item, and Feast deals true damage on a 175-range devour, so the honest advice is spacing, not absorption. The mirror flagged the same phantom shield as a systemic error on Ryze pages.
audit.corrected: Shield claim removed; the level 6+ threat restated as a 175-range true-damage execute that spacing answers and resistances do not.

edits.before: Seraph's Embrace changes the math. Your Flux cascade now ticks fast enough to actually cycle through his resistances, and Realm Warp means you never have to win the side lane — warp your team onto objectives instead. The danger is that Cho'Gath's Feast true damage still executes you through your mana shield if you stand in his face at low HP, so keep the fight mobile: E-root-Q from the edge of his reach, never let him lock you into a still target for a point-blank Rupture at full Feast stacks.
edits.after: Seraph's Embrace changes the math. Your Flux cascade now ticks fast enough to cycle through his resistances, and Realm Warp means you never have to win the side lane — warp your team onto objectives instead. The danger is that Feast is true damage, so no resistance and no shield saves you at low health; it just needs him within 175. Keep the fight long: Flux, root, Overload from the edge of his reach, and never stand still for a point-blank Rupture at full stacks.

notes: Chart flipped to exactly the three rows the mirror proposed (Level 1 Skill, Level 6 Cho'Gath, 2+ items Ryze), as one group with matching ratings. Separately: this page called a 45.61% matchup 'Favoured — difficulty 4/10' with a green tone token while its own chart gave Cho'Gath four of seven stages, so difficulty, carry threat and tone were all corrected. Confirming the mirror's kit note from this side — Cho'Gath's kit file tags Rupture with grounding, but Riot's description says it pops units into the air, so it is a knockup; I wrote knockup throughout and no grounding advice. Ryze's 'mana shield' appears here in whys[6] and late; he has no shield in kit, and I removed the claim rather than re-attribute it to Seraph's, since Feast is true damage and spacing is the real answer.
